items.title: Bandar Utama school murder trial: Defence closes case after boy testifies
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 26 — The defence in the case of a 15-year-old boy charged with murdering a female student at a secondary school in Bandar Utama, Petaling Jaya, last year closed its case today after all defence witnesses had completed their testimony. Judge Adlin Abdul Majid directed the prosecution and defence to file their respective replies on Sept 3, with oral submissions scheduled for Sept 8. Speaking to reporters outside the court, defence lawyer Kitson Foong said the defence had completed its case after two witnesses, including the accused, testified.

items.title: Sabah farmers urged to avoid open burning during Super El Nino
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Farmers in Sabah have been advised against opening new agricultural areas during the expected 'Super' El Nino, said Sabah Agriculture, Fisheries and Food Industry Minister Datuk Jamawi Jaafar. "For the next four to five months, we advise farmers not to open new agricultural areas. Jamawi said Sabah also aimed to increase padi yields to six to seven tonnes per hectare through mechanisation, suitable fertilisers and agricultural technology.

items.title: AHB Holdings sees substantial shareholder exit within two weeks
items.summary: In a Bursa Malaysia filing today, AHB said City Popular disposed of 68 million shares through an off-market transaction on Aug 24, reducing its holding below the substantial shareholder threshold. Based on AHB's closing prices of four sen on Aug 21 and 4.5 sen on Aug 24, the 68 million-share block had a market value of between RM2.72 million and RM3.06 million On Aug 18, AHB disclosed City Popular's emergence as a substantial shareholder after it acquired 99.78 million AHB shares in an off-market transaction on Aug 10. Based solely on the two disclosed transactions, City Popular would have 31.78 million AHB shares remaining after the disposal.

items.title: Ismail Sabri set to face charge over asset declaration tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — Former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob will be charged at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court tomorrow under the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act. Lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad, who represents Ismail Sabri, 66, confirmed to Bernama today that his client would appear in court tomorrow. Amer Hamzah said his client experienced a heart problem while having his statement recorded by MACC on Aug 6.

items.title: Nepal flash flood kills eight; damages roads, power projects
items.summary: KATHMANDU: Nepal sent helicopters to the rescue on Wednesday after a massive flash flood swept away villages in the Himalayan nation, killing eight and damaging roads, bridges and power projects in areas near Tibet, authorities said. Across the border, Tibet reported "major casualties" with some missing in the neighbouring county of Gyirong after a mudslide hit a land crossing between China and Nepal, the Xinhua official news agency said. Nepal's rescue helicopters would be unable to land in the affected areas until the waters recede, however, army spokesperson Raja Ram Basnet said.

items.title: Pengerang peat blaze remains challenging despite water-bombing helicopter support
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI: Firefighters had gained ground in tackling a peat fire along Jalan Bypass Punggai-Sebana Cove in Pengerang here by noon today, with a water-bombing helicopter deployed to support ground operations. Johor Fire and Rescue Department director Siti Rohani Nadir said the weather had caused the fire to spread rapidly, prompting firefighters to maintain round-the-clock operations to contain the flames and prevent further spread. "Hot weather, dry conditions and strong winds have caused the fire to spread quickly," she said.

items.title: Heartbreak and hope as injured elephant ‘Sulong’ treks 100km back to Gua Musang
items.summary: Affectionately named Sulong Chalil, the elephant has drawn widespread sympathy across social media as he treks eastward along the highway shoulder despite nursing an injury to his right front leg. Perhilitan said Sulong remains in stable condition, displaying normal behaviour, feeding regularly, and moving steadily. “Go Sulong go!

items.title: Farrah Naz conferred Datuk title
items.summary: AYER KEROH: Media Prima Berhad News and Current Affairs Deputy Group Managing Editor Datuk Farrah Naz Abd Karim was among the recipients of the Melaka state awards, honours and medals presented in conjunction with the 77th birthday celebration of Yang Dipertua Negeri Melaka Tun Dr Mohd Ali Mohd Rustam today. Farrah Naz, who is also New Straits Times Group Editor, was conferred the Darjah Pangkuan Seri Melaka (DPSM), which carries the title Datuk. She subsequently held several editorial positions at NST, including Putrajaya Bureau Chief, News Editor, Senior News Editor, Associate Editor (News and Current Affairs), NSTtv Editor and Executive Editor (Commercial).

items.title: George Town roads to close for National Day parade from Aug 29–31: Here’s where
items.summary: The Penang Island City Council (MBPP), in a statement today, said the road closures would begin at 2 am on Aug 29 and continue until 1 pm on Aug 31, or until the event concludes, covering several locations in the city centre. “The roads affected include the Chulia Street Ghaut/Weld Quay junction, part of China Street Ghaut, Church Street, the Union Street/Beach Street junction and part of Penang Street from Light Street to Union Street. “Also affected are part of King Street from Bishop Street to Light Street, the Light Street/Kapitan Keling Mosque Road junction and the Tun Syed Sheh Barakbah Road/Light Street junction,” it said.

items.title: Preacher, influencer claims trial to 51 charges involving RM15.4mil
items.summary: SEREMBAN: A preacher and influencer today claimed trial at the Sessions Court here to 34 charges of criminal breach of trust (CBT) involving RM13.8 million belonging to a non-governmental organisation (NGO), and 17 money laundering charges involving RM1.56 million. On the 34 CBT charges, Abdullah, as an agent and chairman of Pertubuhan Rezeki Infaq Malaysia (Prim), was entrusted with RM13,847,535.89 in Prim funds. Abdullah also faces 17 money laundering charges involving RM1.56 million transferred from several bank accounts, including his own, to various accounts to purchase gold.

items.title: Industry body hails Anwar's call for greater creative freedom in films
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Communications and Multimedia Content Forum of Malaysia (CMCF) has welcomed Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's call for Malaysian filmmakers to be given greater creative freedom. It said this should come with stronger self-regulation, clearer content classification and better parental controls. CMCF vice-chairman and Film Directors' Association of Malaysia chairman Datuk Afdlin Shauki said filmmakers needed room to tell difficult or sensitive stories that reflect real life.

items.title: ‘If Muhyiddin did not help me… I would not donate RM4.8m to PPBM’, Bumi contractor says in Jana Wibawa trial
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — A Bumiputera businessman who secured a RM62 million government project under the Jana Wibawa programme told the High Court today that Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin had in 2020 said contractors could donate directly to his political party Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (PPBM). “Also in that meeting, Tan Sri Muhyiddin said spontaneously to me, if there are any PKBM members or contractors who wish to donate, can donate directly to Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia and not to any individuals in PPBM,” Azman said. Azman said that was why he had asked contractors whom he had met and who wished to apply for Jana Wibawa projects to donate directly to Bersatu.

items.title: Govt focused on TH RCI follow-up, not new probes, says Zulkifli
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government's priority following the declassification of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji (TH) is to ensure its findings are acted upon firmly and comprehensively. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the government respected the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) as a credible parliamentary institution and was prepared to provide full cooperation if required. Yesterday, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the PAC should establish a special body to investigate TH's management from 2017 to the present.

items.title: Muhyiddin’s request for Bersatu donations was wrong, Bumiputera contractor chief tells court
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — Then prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin’s July 2020 request for contractors to make donations to his political party Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia during a conversation about government projects for Bumiputera contractors was wrong, a witness told the High Court today. Bumiputera Contractors Association of Malaysia (PKBM) president Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff said this as the prosecution’s 27th witness in Muhyiddin’s power abuse and money laundering trial. Azman said Muhyiddin had spoken about the donations “spontaneously” when he was asking the then Prime Minister about opportunities for government projects for Bumiputera contractors under his association, and that Muhyiddin had also informed him about the Jana Wibawa programme in this meeting.

items.title: Aroundtown's half-year profit more than halves on falling property prices
items.summary: It reported a net profit of €218 million (US$254 million) for the first half of 2026, down 62 per cent from a year ago, due to a lower valuation result and higher financing costs. The property group also posted funds from operations, or FFO I, of €144 million, down from last year's €150 million. Aroundtown had in April guided for its annual FFO I, a key metric measuring real estate firms' operating performance, to come between €275 million and €305 million.

items.title: Tan: Investors turn to collectable art as property market cools
items.summary: "Rather than moving away from property entirely, today's investors simply have a broader selection of asset classes to choose from, including stocks, art, fine wine, cryptocurrency, and even collectibles like premium Chinese tea," Tang said. Tang said rising attendance at art auctions, where collectable pieces can range from about RM10,000 to RM600,000, points to growing interest in alternative assets, particularly when high-quality works by established artists come to market. He said Malaysia's property market was entering a more cautious phase as developers faced mounting construction costs and greater uncertainty over project viability.

items.title: Meta faces possible US$200b penalty as settlement talks emerge
items.summary: SAN FRANCISCO: Social media giant Meta has been in discussions with multiple US states to settle a major child privacy and consumer protection case out of court, Bloomberg News reported on Tuesday. The states are claiming that Meta violated both state-level and federal laws, though the exact allegations vary by state. "Meta Platforms Inc. and state attorneys general have discussed a possible mid-trial settlement," Bloomberg reported, citing anonymous sources familiar with the matter.

items.title: Maternity ward inferno kills 14 infants in Pakistan
items.summary: ISLAMABAD: A fire erupted in a hospital maternity ward in Islamabad on Wednesday killing 14 infants, Pakistan authorities said, blaming a faulty air conditioner for the blaze. The dawn fire broke out on the third floor of the Mother and Child Health Ward at the capital's premier public hospital Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS), the Islamabad district office said in a statement. "The fire spread very quickly.

items.title: Army strengthens capabilities against cross-border threats
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The army is strengthening its capabilities to counter non-conventional threats, including smuggling, intrusion, human trafficking, illegal logging and poaching. He said human trafficking along Malaysia's borders also posed social and demographic security risks, while Sabah's east coast faced maritime threats including piracy and kidnapping for ransom. Malaysia also faced natural resource theft along the peninsula's northern borders and areas bordering Kalimantan, including encroachment into forest reserves, illegal logging and poaching that threatened the country's flora and fauna.

items.title: Preacher, NGO secretary claim trial to RM13.8m CBT and money laundering charges
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 26 — A 40-year-old “religious influencer” claimed trial at the Sessions Court here today to 34 charges of criminal breach of trust (CBT) involving more than RM13.8 million belonging to a non-governmental organisation. Abdullah Abdol Razak, an independent preacher who served as chairman of Pertubuhan Rezeki Infaq Malaysia during the alleged offences, also pleaded not guilty before judge Kunasundary Marimuthu to 17 separate money laundering charges involving RM1.55 million, The Star reported. For Noor Sahira, Deputy Public Prosecutor Syairah Aqilah Khalil proposed bail at RM250,000 with two sureties.

items.title: Taxi driver jailed six years for ramming, killing Rohingya passenger
items.summary: The court also ordered R. Dhana Balan, 31, to serve an additional year in prison if he failed to pay the fine. The victim had travelled from Johor Baru to Batu Pahat with his nephew in Dhana's taxi on Oct 19, 2022. After reaching Batu Pahat, Dhana asked for the fare, but the victim said he did not have enough money.

items.title: No shutdown, but Fahmi says e-commerce platforms to face tighter rules over electrical, halal products
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 26 — The government will take immediate steps to tighten oversight of e-commerce platforms following complaints over products sold online, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. These platforms either have issues involving the products being sold, particularly electrical and electronic equipment, or the halal status of products being offered. He said the MCMC would engage e-commerce platforms, drawing on its experience in regulating social media platforms.

items.title: Alliance Bank Q1 earnings up 25pct as credit loss allowances fall
items.summary: Net profit increased to RM248.32 million from RM198.69 million a year earlier, while revenue grew 2.5 per cent to RM630.93 million from RM615.32 million, according to its Bursa Malaysia filing. NII rose 2.5 per cent year-on-year to RM511.7 million, mainly on higher loan volumes, while net interest margin stood at 2.26 per cent. NOII also increased 2.5 per cent to RM119.2 million.

items.title: Prisons Dept to cooperate in probe into death in Marang prison
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Prisons Department will give full cooperation to police investigating the death of an inmate who was allegedly assaulted by several fellow prisoners at Marang Prison. In a statement today, the department said it had taken note of the incident, in which the inmate lost consciousness after being assaulted by several other inmates. The department said the victim's body was subsequently sent to the Forensic Department of Hospital Sultanah Nur Zahirah (HSNZ), Kuala Terengganu, for a post-mortem examination.

items.title: Thick haze forces rethink of National Day celebrations in Putrajaya, but cancellation not on cards
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 26 — The government is reviewing the scale and location of this year’s National Day celebrations amid the haze affecting several parts of the country, but cancellation is not being considered at this stage, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. The meeting will involve the Communications Ministry, Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry, Meteorological Department, Education Ministry and Health Ministry, among other agencies. Fahmi said the government would assess weather forecasts and projections for the next five to six days, including the expected haze conditions, before making a decision.

items.title: 3 more men remanded over illegal motorcycle race on Johor Second Link
items.summary: KULAI: Three men have been remanded over an illegal motorcycle race on the Second Link highway in Johor, bringing the total number of arrests to 11. A 33-second video showing two motorcyclists racing went viral after several people blocked part of the highway in Johor last Saturday to allow the riders to race. Bukit Aman Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department director Datuk Seri Mohammed Hasbullah Ali said police believed a RM15,000 bet was placed on the illegal motorcycle race.

items.title: Umno denies 'charade' to shield those behind TH scandal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki has rejected allegations that the party staged a "charade" to shield those responsible for financial misconduct at Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH). The response follows criticism from Jelutong Member of Parliament RSN Rayer, who accused Umno of organising a political spectacle to protect individuals involved in the alleged mismanagement of the pilgrims' fund. "Umno has been consistent in our position: we will never condone, defend, or protect anyone found to have committed wrongdoing, whether in the TH issue or any other matter involving public institutions and funds," Asyraf said in a statement.

items.title: [UPDATED] PAC to begin probe into TH governance, financial and investment weaknesses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Parliament's Public Accounts Committee (PAC) today unanimously agreed to begin proceedings into governance, financial and investment weaknesses at Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH). PAC chairman Datuk Wira Mas Ermieyati Samsudin said the decision followed findings in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report into TH's management and operations from 2014 to 2020, which was made public on July 29. She said the proceedings were not intended to duplicate the RCI's comprehensive investigation, but would focus on the actual status and progress of implementing its recommendations, in line with PAC's core function.

items.title: Mi Technovation unit gets nod for Singapore listing
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Mi Technovation Bhd's unit, Mi Material Holding Ltd, has received approval to list on the Singapore Exchange. Mi Technovation will retain an equity interest of about 72.6 per cent in Mi Material following the listing. In a separate filing, Mi Technovation said the listing would enhance Mi Material's recognition and corporate stature.

items.title: Kluang used car dealer claims trial over illegal possession of Smith & Wesson pistol
items.summary: KLUANG, Aug 26 — A used car dealer pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to a charge of possessing a firearm without a valid licence earlier this month. According to the charge sheet, How was alleged to have been in possession of a Smith & Wesson pistol without lawful authorisation at a house in Jalan Indah 2/10, Taman Kluang Indah, at about 6.30 pm on Aug 6. How, together with three other men, was previously charged at the Batu Pahat Magistrate’s Court on Aug 17 with murdering a businessman earlier this month.

items.title: Critical illness can cost Malaysians up to RM1.2mil, says Allianz Life
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Treatment for critical illnesses and related expenses can cost between RM800,000 and RM1.2 million in complex cases, according to Allianz Life Insurance Malaysia Bhd. Chief executive officer Giulio Slavich said the financial burden extended beyond medical bills, with patients potentially facing caregiver costs, loss of income and prolonged treatment. "Critical illness cases are ranging around RM1 million.

items.title: Fall from 63cm can prove fatal - expert
items.summary: Universiti Utara Malaysia (UUM) Risk Management Division deputy director Dr Syazwan Syah Zulkifly said the severity of a fall could not be assessed based on height alone. "Safety management means assessing whether access routes, surfaces, equipment layout and handholds are safe and suitable for workers. He said working conditions could change and new hazards could emerge, requiring risk assessments to be reviewed whenever changes could affect the level of risk.

items.title: Public trust at stake if Audit Department sidelined in TH RCI, says Umno leader
items.summary: © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Dengue deaths rise to 12 in Johor as JB remains hotspot
items.summary: State Health and Environment Committee chairman Ling Tian Soon said Johor Baru remained the state's biggest hotspot, accounting for 492 cases, or 75.6 per cent, followed by Kulai with 115 cases. State data showed 651 cases were reported during Epidemiological Week 33, a 3.4 per cent drop from 674 cases the previous week. No new dengue deaths were reported during the week, but cumulative cases had surged 119.6 per cent to 9,290 as of Aug 23, from 4,231 during the corresponding period last year.

items.title: Penang tycoon Tan Kok Ping loses libel appeal against CM Chow Kon Yeow, ordered to pay RM50,000
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 26 — The Court of Appeal here today upheld the High Court’s dismissal of businessman Tan Sri Tan Kok Ping’s libel suit against Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow. A three-member bench comprising Justices Datuk Dr Alwi Abdul Wahab, Datuk Dr Shahnaz Sulaiman and Datuk Amarjeet Singh unanimously dismissed Tan’s appeal against the Nov 26, 2024 High Court decision. The court ordered Tan to pay RM50,000 in costs.

items.title: [UPDATED] Govt considering regulatory framework for e-commerce platforms
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Communications Ministry and Finance Ministry are exploring a regulatory framework for e-commerce platforms following public complaints about the safety standards and halal compliance of products sold online, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said. "Thus, the prime minister has instructed the Finance Ministry and the Communications Ministry to look into immediate measures to implement regulatory processes, including registration requirements for e-commerce platforms," he said at a press conference here today. Fahmi said the government aimed to ensure that all electrical and electronic goods sold online carried SIRIM certification, while food products strictly complied with local halal standards.

items.title: Man sentenced to 30 years' jail, 12 strokes for murder
items.summary: Judge Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid handed down the sentence after finding Lim Yew Lung, 32, guilty of murdering Tsun Chin Kiang, 43. He also found that the accused's defence, as well as those of two defence witnesses, failed to raise any reasonable doubt. Meor Hashimi ordered the 30-year sentence to run from the date of Lim's arrest on Jan 29, 2020.

items.title: Public Bank Q2 net profit up 3.7pct, declares 10.5 sen dividend
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Public Bank Bhd's net profit rose 3.7 per cent to RM1.82 billion in the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, from RM1.76 billion a year earlier, as revenue increased 3.5 per cent to RM7.61 billion from RM7.35 billion. In a bourse filing, Public Bank said the improved performance was mainly supported by higher non-interest income, which grew RM165.7 million, or 21.3 per cent, on stronger unit trust sales and higher unit trust management fee income. For the first half of 2026, net profit increased 2.02 per cent to RM3.58 billion from RM3.51 billion a year earlier, while revenue rose 1.7 per cent to RM14.93 billion from RM14.67 billion.

items.title: Lynas expands global footprint, eyes new rare earths supply deals
items.summary: MELBOURNE: Australia's Lynas Rare Earths said it planned to grow its global supply chain on Wednesday, with discussions to secure new mine supply from project developers around the world and set up a magnet processing facility in the United States. The comments came after the world's biggest producer of rare earths outside China reported a sharp rise in annual profit, helped by record average selling prices for rare-earth oxide and strong demand, but missed market expectations. Interim chief executive officer (CEO) Pol Le Roux said Lynas is in talks with project developers of ionic clay deposits around the world for new supply and expects to announce new deals soon.

items.title: [UPDATED] Govt to decide today on National Day celebrations amid haze
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The government will decide whether to adjust the scale and venue of the 2026 National Day celebrations amid deteriorating air quality caused by haze nationwide, says Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar would make the decision following discussions with the Communications Ministry, Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry, Malaysian Meteorological Department, Education Ministry and Health Ministry. "A decision will be reached today," he said at a press conference here today.

items.title: Father, 9-year-old son found dead hugging in house fire
items.summary: KUALA NERUS: A man and his nine-year-old son were found dead in an embrace after they were trapped in a house fire at Kampung Tok Jembal, here. The victims were identified as Amirulfahmi Wan Jusoh, 40, and his son, Rehan Yusuf, 9. "My wife shouted that a house was on fire.

items.title: Jakim to hold special prayers tonight as haze blankets Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — The Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim) will hold a Solat Hajat (special prayer of needs) at three mosques under its supervision tonight following the haze currently affecting the country. Jakim director-general Datuk Dr Sirajuddin Suhaimee said the prayers would be held after Maghrib prayers at the National Mosque here, as well as Putra Mosque and Tuanku Mizan Zainal Abidin Mosque in Putrajaya. “May Allah SWT protect all Malaysians from any harm, safeguard our health and safety and restore conditions in affected areas,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Bersatu Youth chief hints at possible cooperation with Selangor government
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — Bersatu Youth chief Hilman Idham has suggested that his party could back Pakatan Harapan in the Selangor government until the end of its current term. “Bersatu has worked with all political parties before, including BN and Harapan. Former Selangor MB and current Hulu Kelang assemblyman Datuk Seri Azmin Ali, who heads Selangor PN, currently leads Bersatu in the state assembly.

items.title: MMEA clears Karakit-Kudat ferry after passenger safety concerns go viral
items.summary: KUDAT, Aug 26 — The Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) Kudat Zone conducted an inspection of a ferry operating on the Karakit-Kudat route on Sunday following information circulating on social media concerning the safety and comfort of its passengers. MMEA Kudat Zone Director Maritime Commander Hasbullah Omar said the inspection was conducted to ensure ferry operators consistently complied with safety requirements and relevant regulations. He said MMEA Kudat Zone took all information and complaints received from the public seriously, particularly those concerning passenger safety and vessel operations in Kudat waters.

items.title: Calls grow for Sabah to widen pork imports beyond Denmark and France as prices climb to RM18 per kg
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 26 — Pork prices in Sabah have risen to RM17.50 or RM18 per kg, prompting calls for wider import sources and stronger efforts to reduce food costs in the State. Agriculture and Food Security Deputy Minister Datuk Chan Foong Hin said the increase was partly linked to Sabah’s limited sources of imported pork, with the State currently allowing imports from only Denmark and France. “Sabah only allows two countries – Denmark and France,” he said, adding that all imported pork sources must first undergo audits and meet food safety requirements.

items.title: High Court refuses to strike out RM200,000 fee refund suit against Sri Ram’s estate
items.summary: Khoo engaged Sri Ram in 2022 as lead counsel to represent his son, Adrian Khoo, in a criminal appeal before the Court of Appeal. A pro forma invoice issued by Sri Ram’s law firm, Messrs Sri Ram, fixed the legal fees at RM349,800, after which Gee Tat made four instalment payments totalling RM200,000. He filed the present lawsuit against Sri Ram’s widow, Chandra Sri Ram, in her capacity as the executor and trustee of the late judge’s estate.

items.title: Woman, 62, found bound and dead in Sandakan, cops nab 10 suspects, youngest aged 10
items.summary: District Police Chief ACP George Abd Rahman said the woman, believed to have been living alone, was found with her hands tied behind her back and her head covered with a piece of cloth inside the house’s toilet. George said the victim was identified through documents found in the house. George said two were identified as main suspects.

items.title: Sabah to upgrade SICC-Menera Kinabalu stretch, ditch permanent bridge plan
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 26 — The State Government plans to upgrade the entire stretch from the Sabah International Convention Centre (SICC) towards Menara Kinabalu, making the permanent replacement of the bridge at Tanjung Lipat unnecessary. Deputy Chief Minister I cum State Works and Utilities Minister Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam said this when asked whether there were any plans to repair the bridge. The Bailey bridge was opened to the public last Friday.

items.title: Putrajaya approves 367 projects worth RM9b to replace dilapidated schools
items.summary: TAPAH, Aug 26 — The government has approved 367 projects to redevelop dilapidated school buildings worth RM9 billion nationwide from 2023 to 2026. Deputy Education Minister Wong Kah Woh said the allocation involved 86 projects worth RM1.711 billion in 2023, 78 projects totalling RM1.825 billion in 2024, 124 projects costing RM4.1 billion in 2025 and 79 projects worth RM1.384 billion in 2026. He said this when met after attending the handover ceremony for the Education Ministry’s Dilapidated School Replacement Building Project at Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan Cina (SJKC) Coldstream here today.

items.title: Penang State Museum smashes 2026 visitor targets in first month after reopening
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 26 — The Penang State Museum on Farquhar Street has recorded a surge of 47,638 visitors in just 29 days following its reopening last month, exceeding initial expectations. “Our original target was 30,000 visitors by December, but in one month we have already exceeded 47,000 visitors,” Wong said at a press conference at the museum today. The museum’s peak attendance occurred on Aug 9, with 3,750 visitors in a single day.

items.title: Stop shifting goalposts on Tabung Haji RCI, PKR Youth tells Akmal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — PKR Youth information chief Danish Hairudin has accused Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Akmal Saleh of shifting his stance on the Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) because its findings and resulting arrests failed to match his political narrative. “Must everyone follow Akmal and Umno’s lead until we get the answer that Umno wants?” “Reveal everything.

items.title: Missing Penang Kafa teacher due to wed in September turns up in Kedah
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 26 — A male Quran and Fardu Ain (Kafa) teacher who was reported missing since last Saturday after leaving his home at an apartment in Sungai Ara near here was found safe in Kampung Bukit Payong, Pokok Sena, Kedah early this morning. Barat Daya police chief ACP Anuwal Ab Wahab said following further investigations, police managed to trace Mohamad Hijazi Zamri, 26, at a house in Kampung Bukit Payong. Previously, police said investigations found that the man had asked his mother for permission to go to Surau Al-Muttaqin in Lilitan Sungai Ara on a blue Yamaha LC135 motorcycle.

items.title: Coroner walks out during Zara Qairina inquest after saying ‘Am I not fair enough?’ twice
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 26 — The Coroner’s Court hearing the inquest into the death of Zara Qairina Mahathir saw a tense moment today when Coroner Judge Amir Shah Amir Hassan suddenly stood and left his bench after twice asking, “Am I not fair enough?” Datuk Rizwandean M. Borhan, representing Zara Qairina’s mother, then remarked that Ram’s questioning of Wong appeared harsh. Ram then said: “No, Sir.

items.title: Kuching airport repairs underway after storm damages ceiling
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 26 — Repair works have been carried out at Kuching International Airport (KIA) following damage to part of its external ceiling structure caused by severe weather on Tuesday. Malaysia Airports, in an update posted on its official Facebook page, said the affected area had been secured to allow the repair works to be carried out safely. “Repair works at KIA are underway on the section of the external ceiling structure affected by the severe weather earlier today (Tuesday),” it said.

items.title: Look beyond racial and political lines this Merdeka, urges Sultan of Selangor
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 26 — The Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, has urged Malaysians to use this year’s National Day celebrations to reinforce national unity by looking past racial, religious, and political divides. The Sultan had earlier consented to the Jalur Gemilang being hoisted at the Selangor State Flagpole throughout the commemorative period. “Although we differ in race, religion, language, political ideology and background, the Jalur Gemilang reminds us that we remain citizens of the same nation,” the Sultan said.

items.title: WhatsApp ‘boss’ scam leaves Terengganu car dealership RM452,000 poorer
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Aug 26 — A car dealership company suffered losses of RM452,000 after its clerk fell victim to a phone scam syndicate. Kuala Terengganu district police chief ACP Azli Mohd Noor said the 50-year-old finance clerk received a WhatsApp message last Monday from a suspect whom she believed to be the company owner. He said the suspect instructed the victim to provide the company’s account balance and make three separate transfers totalling RM452,000 to three different accounts on the same day.

items.title: Penang SPM candidate targeted in sexual cyberbullying gets Education Dept support, protection
items.summary: Its director Mohamad Dziauddin Mat Saad said appropriate steps had been taken to protect the identity of the 17-year-old student and ensure that the incident did not disrupt her preparations for the SPM examination. Mohamad Dziauddin said the school had also advised the student to seek guidance and counselling to help her manage her emotions and focus on her SPM preparations. He said JPNPP would continue to monitor the case and work with the school and parents to safeguard the student’s safety and wellbeing.

items.title: One China policy: Understanding Malaysia’s position on Beijing and Taipei
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s remarks on Taiwan have brought renewed attention to Malaysia’s One China policy and its relations with Beijing and Taipei. Anwar later reiterated that Malaysia prefers a peaceful resolution and that its position under the One China policy remains unchanged since 1974. What is the ‘One China’ framework?

items.title: Three more nabbed over illegal race on Malaysia-Singapore Second Link
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — Police have arrested three more men in Kuala Lumpur over a brazen illegal street race that brought traffic to a halt along the Malaysia-Singapore Second Link. Kulai police chief Tan Seng Lee said the latest arrests bring the total number of individuals detained in connection with the incident to 11, Kosmo reported. Police had earlier rounded up eight men on Sunday, including a motorsport influencer, obtaining a four-day remand order to facilitate investigations.

items.title: Bersatu leadership approves two Pahang reps’ move to back Umno menteri besar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 26 — Two Bersatu assemblymen in Pahang have thrown their support behind Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail of Umno, with the party's top leadership signalling its backing for the move. Kuala Sentul assemblyman Datuk Jasri Jamaluddin and Lepar assemblyman Datuk Mohd Yazid Mohd Yunus — Bersatu's only two elected representatives in the 42-seat Pahang assembly — signed a memorandum of understanding with Wan Rosdy, pledging their backing for his administration until the next state election, expected by early 2028. Wan Rosdy has headed the Pahang state government since a hung assembly emerged from the November 2022 state election.
